# ScreenGui

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ScreenGui")`

The root of one screen-space UI tree, parented to `UIService` (§2.2). Everything under it is laid out against the window and drawn over the world.

It is the unit of layout: a write that changes a layout marks the nearest ScreenGui dirty, and a screen nothing changed does not run the solver at all. That is a design constraint rather than an optimisation -- the benchmark asserts ZERO solver invocations on an idle frame, because "about zero microseconds" is a measurement of the clock.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DisplayOrder` | `number` | `0` | read/write | Which ScreenGui draws on top when two overlap, highest last. `ZIndex` orders WITHIN a tree and this orders BETWEEN trees, so a HUD and a modal never have to agree on a shared numbering. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this tree is laid out and drawn at all. A disabled ScreenGui costs one boolean read per frame; it does not cost a layout. |
| `KeepOnSceneLoad` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether this screen goes with the game to the next scene (ADR 0106) rather than with the scene it is in. A loading screen drawn before `SceneService:LoadScene` stays up while the scene changes under it, and a script takes it down on `SceneLoaded`. |
| `ReferenceHeight` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The height of the window this tree was laid out for, or 0 for pixels. With one set, every offset, text size, corner and stroke under it is in units of a window that tall, and the engine scales the whole tree to the window it has -- so a layout drawn for a 720-line monitor takes the same share of a phone with twice the lines, where in pixels it would be half its size. The width follows: the window is as many units wide as its shape gives that height, so anchor to edges with `Scale` and size with `Offset`. `AbsolutePosition` and `AbsoluteSize` stay in window pixels. 720 suits a layout drawn on a desktop. |
| `ScreenInsets` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this tree lays out inside `UIService.SafeAreaInsets` rather than against the whole window. On by default: a full-bleed background is the exception and a HUD clipped by a notch is the failure. |
